title: Do Bumblebees Play? Balls Without a Food Reward | Toxic Tales
description:
Why would a bumblebee roll a wooden ball when there is no food reward?

In laboratory experiments, Bombus terrestris bumblebees repeatedly rolled balls despite having a clear route to food. In a separate age test, younger bees rolled more often. A colour-chamber experiment also suggested that the activity itself could be rewarding.

The researchers interpreted the behaviour as play-like. These laboratory tests do not directly reveal how bees feel or establish how often wild bees do this. The age and colour tests used separate experimental groups.

TT-007 | Original research:
Galpayage Dona et al. (2022). Do bumble bees play? Animal Behaviour 194:239-251.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.anbehav.2022.08.013
